content:
We (@Joe Stubbs and I) started the project Sequencelib (see website, and github repository): a platform for formalizing sequences from The On-line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences.

The main goals of the project are:

  • Providing a unified API for defining integer sequences from the OEIS, with some extra ergonomics around it: automatic linking to the OEIS pages, collecting values, and collecting proofs of equivalences among sequences. We have plans for extending these tools, such as adding automatic theorems for initial values (when those can be proved in straightforward ways). We are very open to suggestions as well.

  • Providing a space for people to experiment with a wide range of formalizations. We are following Mathlib in terms of syntactic style (see our contributing guidelines), but we welcome formalizations of objects that might not be in the most general or abstract form. We consider the the main API of the project to be the sequences and the theorems about their values and equivalences. Any definitions of concepts or theorems that are necessary for defining a sequence are welcome, whether in its most general context, or in a specialized context that is enough for the definition of the sequence. Theorems about properties of the sequences are also welcome (similar to the content in sections “Comments”, “Formula”, “Example”, etc. in OEIS).

There are already twelve core OEIS sequences in the repository that illustrate the points above. We would love to hear feedback from people, and hopefully get some contributions! 

(Note: This project started after discussion and consensus that a PR containing some results on Sylvester’s sequence were out of scope for Mathlib. See the original discussion here.)
